claims.text: Substituting a portion of heavy metallic elements with lightweight elements such as Be or Mg reduces alloy density.
Controlled Be or Mg substitution promotes formation of a uniform solid solution.
Controlled Be or Mg substitution facilitates in situ formation of stable, passivating oxide scales at high temperature.
The passivating oxide scales allow mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance to be maintained or enhanced.
Lightweight-element substitution produces a more homogeneous solid solution.
Lightweight-element substitution encourages formation of a fine-scale protective surface oxide enriched in lightweight elements.
The lightweight elements have oxidation properties favorable to forming stable, passivating oxide scales.
Stable, passivating oxide scales inhibit further surface degradation during high-temperature exposure.
High configurational entropy supports an overall uniform microstructure.
A uniform microstructure helps preserve mechanical and corrosion-resistant properties.
Within an optimal substitution range, modified alloys will have lower density than the baseline while maintaining or enhancing mechanical strength.
Within an optimal substitution range, modified alloys will maintain or enhance corrosion resistance relative to the baseline.
Within an optimal substitution range, modified alloys will maintain or enhance high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the baseline.
Excessive lightweight-element content may introduce defects or brittle intermetallic phases.
Defects, brittle intermetallic phases, phase separation, or unstable oxide scales caused by excessive substitution will degrade the combined properties.
